statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. With CME equity index futures shut since Friday 21:00 UTC there is no live Nasdaq-100 price path to score, so Tail stays far below the block threshold, while Stress remains elevated on an unresolved US-Iran naval exchange around the Strait of Hormuz, a tightening blockade and an OPEC+ quota rollover that adds no supply offset.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 22:00-02:00 UTC futures-reopen window rather than across the whole outlook; existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: No live Nasdaq-100 price path five hours before the 22:00 UTC reopen, with CENTCOM reporting 92 commercial vessels redirected under the Iran blockade and OPEC+ leaving October quotas unchanged
body: CME equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00 UTC, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path is observable at this assessment. The last verified tape remains Friday September 4: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,544.15 (+0.21%) inside a 29,440.15-29,655.22 range against a 29,482.30 previous close, a mid-range finish with no session-extreme hold, while the front NQ future settled near 29,565. VIX ended at 14.53 after a contained 13.80-14.58 day range. Friday's internals were rotational rather than directional, with semiconductors broadly higher while several megacaps fell, which argues against an aligned one-way regime being carried into the reopen. Two verified developments have been added since the previous hour. CENTCOM reported that US forces have redirected 92 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two under the naval blockade of Iran, an update posted this afternoon and following Saturday's strikes on three IRGC-linked tankers after ballistic missiles were fired toward a US carrier and destroyer. Separately, OPEC+ met on Sunday and left October output quotas unchanged, pausing its unwinding of the 1.65 million barrel-per-day cut, so no additional supply is scheduled to offset the Hormuz disruption. Brent finished Friday at $96.28 with crude up more than 9% on the week, its strongest week since mid-July, and H.15 for September 3 shows the 2-year at 4.34%, the 10-year at 4.77% and the 30-year at 5.25%. That combination keeps Stress elevated. It does not move Tail, because Tail measures an observed pathological price path and no price path exists while the venue is shut. Conditional risk is therefore concentrated in the 22:00-02:00 UTC reopen, when a two-day headline backlog meets the thinnest depth of the week; that window maps to WATCH rather than to a block, since gap risk without observed extension is not evidence of mean-reversion failure. Monday is the US Labor Day holiday: US cash markets are closed, CME equity index futures trade a shortened session ending 17:00 UTC, and the US data calendar is empty until Tuesday.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available. Tail held in a narrow 4-5 band with EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress oscillated between 51 and 57 across the weekend closure, easing through the Asian overnight and firming again across the European and US Sunday hours to finish the window at 57. Confidence stayed in an 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal for every hour, reflecting a closed venue rather than an observed regime.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover five further closed hours, the scheduled 22:00 UTC futures reopen, and an Asian and European session on a US Labor Day holiday with no US cash open inside the window. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band except for the two hours around the reopen, which reach 23 and 21 and map to WATCH where the unresolved Hormuz escalation, the tightening blockade and a stretched energy complex would meet the thinnest depth of the week, before decaying toward 8 as two-way discovery is assumed to resume. Stress peaks near 66 at the reopen on the combined rates and energy backdrop before unwinding toward 51. No US macro release falls inside the window; the next high-impact checkpoints are PPI on September 10 and CPI on September 11.
